arxiv.title: SwapBot: Tool-Centric Robot Manipulation via Interchangeable End-Effectors and Tactile Sensing
arxiv.abstract: Robot manipulation in everyday environments inherently involves substantial tool usage. Seemingly simple household tasks, such as cooking pan-fried tofu, require forceful cutting, delicate brushing, and precise placement using different tools under contact-rich interaction. Thus, the ability to autonomously swap and use task-appropriate tools is important for tool-centric manipulation. We introduc

arxiv.title: SymAnt: Grounding Long-Horizon Action Anticipation with Adaptable Symbolic Priors
arxiv.abstract: As robots and intelligent systems increasingly interact with humans, they must anticipate long sequences of future actions from only brief observations. While purely neural models typically require extensive observations to predict future actions and remain difficult to interpret and adjust, symbolic priors offer a structured alternative. To this end, we introduce SymAnt, a novel neuro-symbolic ap

arxiv.title: A Conveyor Belt Mechanism for Repositionable Magnetic Coupling Between Continuum Robots
arxiv.abstract: This work proposes a novel conveyor belt mechanism enabling continuous, active repositioning of functional elements along the body of a tendon-driven continuum robot. Up to three conveyor belt mechanisms are integrated within a 9 mm diameter continuum robot. We demonstrate equivalent or reduced conveyor belt actuation forces compared to robot tendon actuation forces. As a case study, we mount perm

arxiv.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents
arxiv.abstract: Realistic, fast robotics simulations could enable large-scale training of embodied AI models that transfer to the real world. However, despite decades of progress, available simulations cover only a narrow range of real-world tasks and physical phenomena. The core bottleneck is that creating better simulations requires significant expert effort and therefore does not scale. To address this, we int

arxiv.title: A Tutorial on Shape Servoing of Deformable Objects-Part I: Fundamentals
arxiv.abstract: In robotics, shape control (or shape servoing) refers to the automatic manipulation of a deformable object to achieve a desired shape. It involves a feedback loop that exploits the relation between robot motion and changes in the measured shape. arxiv.title: PhysVLMM: Interaction-Conditioned Physical Belief Maps for Articulated Objects in Robot Scene Maps
arxiv.abstract: Mobile robots must open doors and drawers, yet their scene maps record what each object is and whether it has moved, not how it will respond to a pull. This paper proposes PhysVLMM, a method that maintains a physical belief for every articulated part of a Vision-Language-Motion Map and answers a planner's queries about it, with two algorithms: a map update and a query. arxiv.title: DAWN: Diffusion-based Alignment and unfastening Workflow Network
arxiv.abstract: We present DAWN (Diffusion-based Alignment and unfastening Workflow Network), a hierarchical robotic framework designed to perform real-world, unfastening tasks through multi-modal sensory integration. arxiv.title: BURGER: Benchmarking and Understanding Robotic Generalization via Embodied Drawing
arxiv.abstract: How effectively can vision-language-action (VLA) models learn diverse language-conditioned behaviors as training data scales? Investigating this question requires large and varied robot datasets, whose collection on physical robots remains costly. arxiv.title: A Two-Wheeled Quadrotor with All-Clockwise Tilted Rotors for Level-Attitude Surface Locomotnion
arxiv.abstract: Conventional wheel-equipped quadrotor UAVs must tilt their bodies to generate lateral forces, limiting their ability to maintain a desired attitude during lateral motion. This paper proposes a wheeled quadrotor with all-clockwise tilted rotors that uses surface contact as a constraint to generate propulsion along the contact surface without tilting the vehicle. arxiv.title: Fundamental Limits of Sampling-Based Reachability: Geometry and Flow Distortion
arxiv.abstract: Sampling-based reachability estimates reachable sets from finitely many simulated trajectory endpoints. Existing guarantees often control missed probability mass or approximation error relative to the convex hull of the reachable set, leaving the geometric error relative to the reachable set incompletely characterized. We study this error as a problem of support estimation under flow distortion. O

arxiv.title: Adaptive search with path-constrained mobile sensors using multi-arm bandits
arxiv.abstract: We study a constrained sequential decision problem for detecting regions of interest from noisy online measurements collected by a team of energy-constrained mobile sensors. The sensor motion is restricted to a precomputed set of feasible paths that satisfy mobility constraints, limited available energy by requiring return to charging stations, and avoidance of known obstacles. arxiv.title: Improving Fine-Grained Manipulation through Demonstration Expansion and Execution Design
arxiv.abstract: Fine-grained manipulation requires a robot policy to follow instructions, remain robust to visual variations, and translate predicted actions into precise robot control. We present Demonstration Expansion and Execution Design (DEED), a framework for adapting a pretrained vision-language-action policy to the five MetaFine tasks through structured demonstration expansion and execution design. arxiv.title: Optimal Path Planning with Localization constraints
arxiv.abstract: This paper studies UAV path planning in areas where GPS signals are not present. Because these drones can easily get lost when they don't have GPS, they must rely on dead reckoning and occasionally pass near cellular towers, which act as landmarks to reset and fix their position. The goal is to find the shortest path from a start to a goal location while keeping the estimation uncertainty within a

arxiv.title: socx: GPU-Accelerated Chance-Constrained Stochastic Optimal Control using JAX
arxiv.abstract: In this article, we present socx, a GPU-accelerated solver for lifted convex reformulations of linear stochastic optimal control under chance constraints, implemented in JAX. We demonstrate that by exploiting the sparse and independent structure of the problem, distributed optimization can reduce it to simpler problems: independent linear-quadratic tracking (LQT) problems and Euclidean projections

arxiv.title: Continuous-Action World Models: Learning Cross-Embodiment Spatiotemporal Dynamics Priors
arxiv.abstract: We introduce Continuous-Action World Models (CoAWM), a framework for learning cross-embodiment spatiotemporal dynamics priors that support robot action generation across embodiments and execution frequencies. arxiv.title: Propose-Filter-Release: Scaling Noise to Typical Sensitivity via Private Filtering
arxiv.abstract: An estimator can be accurate and stable on typical data, yet sensitive to a few possible records. Differentially private mechanisms commonly scale their noise to the worst-case influence of a single record, which lets these records dictate the noise even when the remaining data would allow far less. arxiv.title: Rethinking Neural Thickets Without Weight Perturbations
arxiv.abstract: The Neural Thickets hypothesis posits that pretrained language models lie in dense neighborhoods of task-specific experts in weight space, which random Gaussian perturbations can uncover. We reproduce the reported gains, but show that they do not require this geometric explanation. arxiv.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
arxiv.abstract: Pixel-space generative Transformers typically use one token per image patch, so capturing finer detail requires more tokens and makes global attention increasingly expensive. We observe that finer detail does not necessarily require more global communication: low-frequency structure benefits from global exchange, while high-frequency detail can be modeled locally. arxiv.title: Adaptive Scenario Generation for KL-DRO Around a Learned Density Model
arxiv.abstract: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) hedges data-driven two-stage stochastic programs against error in the distribution estimated from a finite record, and standard ambiguity sets differ in how they treat realizations absent from that record. arxiv.title: world2vec: Mechanistic world models through latent dynamics learning
arxiv.abstract: World models can achieve strong control performance without faithfully capturing the dynamics of their environment, limiting their potential for mechanistic interpretability and scientific discovery. Here, we introduce world2vec to learn mechanistic world models without reward information directly from observations and actions. arxiv.title: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models
arxiv.abstract: The marginals of a continuous diffusion model can be reproduced by a deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE), known as the probability flow ODE, which provides a foundation for accelerated sampling and consistency distillation. arxiv.title: Difficulty Calibration Across Time for Membership Inference in Diffusion Models
arxiv.abstract: Modern diffusion models are trained on massive datasets that often include copyrighted or private images. Membership inference attacks (MIAs) address this by testing whether a given image was in a model's training set. arxiv.title: Multistatic ISAC with Deep Learning-Based Clutter Suppression for 5G and Beyond
arxiv.abstract: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems using 5G and beyond signals of opportunity enable joint wireless sensing and communication using shared infrastructure and spectrum resources. arxiv.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
arxiv.abstract: Foundation models are typically trained in stages: pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), with changes in both data and learning algorithms. We show that this algorithmic separation is not fundamental. arxiv.title: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Mobile Money Scan Messages in Ghana: A Comparative Evaluation of Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, and Randon Forest Classifiers
arxiv.abstract: Mobile money (MoMo) is Ghana's preferred retail payment channel, recording GHC518.4 billion in transactions in December 2025 and over 26.7 million active accounts (Graphic Online, 2026). arxiv.title: TRACER, a time-to-event EHR foundation model for disease detection across health systems
arxiv.abstract: Foundation models trained on longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) can predict clinical diagnoses years in the future, making them a potential tool for disease screening. We developed TRACER (Temporal Risk Assessment with Clinical EHR Representations), a decoder-based foundation model pretrained on data from over 4.5 million patients from four health systems, and evaluated it on 16 inciden

arxiv.title: Homebrewed SLMs: Autoregressive and Masked Diffusion Language Models Built at Home for Portuguese
arxiv.abstract: Building a language model of one's own no longer requires a data centre. This tutorial trains one from scratch, tokenizer included, on one consumer GPU, and shows how to tell whether it is good for the tasks of a specialist domain. It proposes no new method. arxiv.title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations
arxiv.abstract: We introduce NEOPIC, a framework for learning the field operator in particle-based methods applied to kinetic plasma simulations. Its key novelty is a neural operator that acts directly on the empirical measure of the particles, rather than on a grid, and is evaluated at the particle positions. No mesh or tree is needed and, unlike grid-based neural operators, no deposition onto a mesh takes place

arxiv.title: How I Aligned Your Model: Scaling Up Multilingual Safety Training with Templates
arxiv.abstract: Safety alignment for Large Language Models is heavily focused on English with limited multilingual representation, particularly damaging low-resource language performance. Related open training datasets are often limited in size or do not follow region-localized harmful topics to broaden the scope of alignment beyond cultures. arxiv.title: LRMoE: Demand-Side Load Re-Calibration for Efficient MoE Training on Memory-Constrained Nodes
arxiv.abstract: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models offer scalable capacity for Web applications, but uneven routing creates computation and communication bottlenecks. Existing placement and replication methods redistribute this workload, yet additional expert copies compete with token-related buffers for limited GPU memory. We present LRMoE, a memory-aware MoE training system that jointly recalibrates backwar

arxiv.title: Amortized Localized Posterior Inference for Model Calibration with Application to an Ocean Turbulence Closure
arxiv.abstract: Model discrepancy may prevent a single calibration parameter from reproducing a physical response across the context domain. In addition, uncertainties in observations and contexts affect calibration and must be accounted for and quantified. We construct a family of localized posteriors by weighting observation likelihoods according to their proximity to a target context. Gaussian localization wei

arxiv.title: ThinkJev: One Thought, Every Budget for Calibrated Typed Decisions
arxiv.abstract: Many uses of language models end in a typed decision: a choice among a closed set of options, whose probabilities code can act on. Reading those probabilities from one forward pass is fast but often wrong on decisions that take several steps, such as arithmetic, counting, and date comparison. Letting the model think first fixes most of these errors, but costs seconds per decision instead of millis

arxiv.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
arxiv.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. We introduce OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary resource that combines a structured corpus of open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of recently resolved pr

arxiv.title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
arxiv.abstract: Web agents require diverse, executable, and resettable website environments for reproducible training and evaluation. Human-assisted mirrors demand per-site engineering, while generative construction can diverge from specified real websites. Capture-and-replay preserves observations, with interaction coverage constrained by captured content and replay capabilities. We present WebAnything, a fully

arxiv.title: What Does an Ontology Catch? Curated, LLM-Generated and Data-Derived Ontologies as Checkers of LLM Agents over Knowledge Graphs
arxiv.abstract: LLM agents that answer questions over Web knowledge graphs are increasingly wrapped in checks derived from the graph's ontology, on the assumption that a formal schema makes a reliable judge. Yet a checker can be wrong as well: it can miss errors, and it can flag correct answers and push the agent into "fixing" them. Whether a curated ontology is worth its cost as such a judge, and how it compares

arxiv.title: Measuring Where Intent Gets Lost in Agentic Smart Contract Synthesis
arxiv.abstract: AI agents can now write software from a plain-English description, but code that runs is not the same as code that does what was asked. This gap matters most for smart contracts, the programs behind Web3 applications that move money on a blockchain and cannot be fixed once deployed. We ask how to check whether an AI-written contract behaves as it should, and where the requested behavior gets lost.

arxiv.title: Detecting Covert Collusion between AI Agents through Partner-Outsider Positive Listening
arxiv.abstract: AI agents that share a secret convention can coordinate through messages that look innocent, so a monitor that reads only the messages can miss them. We propose a behavioural test: a partner that uses a code reacts to the exact wording of a message, whereas an uninvolved agent placed in its seat does not. arxiv.title: Evaluating and improving AI agents for sequencing protocol understanding
arxiv.abstract: Existing scientific-agent benchmarks rarely evaluate whether agents can reconstruct the exact molecular structures and generation workflows specified by sequencing protocols, a capability critical for analyzing customized sequencing assays. We introduce LibStructBench, a document-grounded benchmark for reconstructing sequencing-library structures and molecular workflows. Our experiments show that

arxiv.title: Seq@K: Evaluating Language Models Under Sequential Feedback
arxiv.abstract: Language-model agents differ fundamentally from prior intelligent systems in their ability to learn from natural language in context. This capability enables agents to iteratively refine their answers in response to feedback, a prevalent mode of operation in modern agentic workflows. arxiv.title: What Constitutes Food Similarity? Visual Representations and Retrieval in Indian Cuisine
arxiv.abstract: Food similarity underlies retrieval, recommendation, substitution, and other food computing tasks, yet food representations are typically evaluated by identity preservation. We ask what happens to food similarity beyond identity: how different visual representations organize foods into relational neighborhoods, what culinary relationships these neighborhoods reveal or obscure, and how consistently

arxiv.title: Verification Learning Theory: A Process Model of Checking and Retention in AI-Assisted Judgment
arxiv.abstract: Accurate AI assistance can improve immediate judgments while reducing opportunities to practise the operations needed for independent performance. Verification Learning Theory (VLT) formalises this possibility for claim-evaluation practice followed by correct, independent, rule-specific feedback. The model links perceived assistant reliability to evidence checking and links the history of those ch

arxiv.title: The Anatomy of Socio-Demographics in Pluralistic Offensiveness Modeling: When and Where It Helps, and the Role of Reasoning
arxiv.abstract: Subjective judgments such as offensiveness often vary substantially across individuals, motivating pluralistic modeling approaches that incorporate annotators' socio-demographic information to capture this variation. However, prior findings on the benefits of socio-demographic information for pluralistic modeling are mixed, calling for a systematic analysis of both its effectiveness and the mechan

arxiv.title: FilingLoop: Evaluating and Evolving LLM Agents for Corporate Disclosure Review and Revision
arxiv.abstract: Public disclosure repositories such as SEC EDGAR support informed investment through web access to corporate filings. Supporting their review with language model agents requires discovering unstated deficiencies across related documents, acquiring missing company facts, and verifying that requested revisions satisfy evidence-backed requirements. Existing financial question-answering evaluations pr

arxiv.title: Beyond Low-Pass Dynamics: Frequency-Selective Spiking Reservoirs with Resonant Neurons
arxiv.abstract: Spiking reservoir computing combines the training efficiency of fixed recurrent reservoirs with the energy efficiency of event-driven inference, where computation is triggered by sparse spikes rather than executed densely at every timestep. arxiv.title: Micro-Edits: Computational Support for Fine-Scale Edits in Film
arxiv.abstract: In film editing, every frame matters. While macro, content-level edits shape the high-level narrative of a film, small local edits often control timing and direct visual attention. For example, editors can adjust the precise timing of clips to control the length of a meaningful silence, or cut to shots that highlight a specific character's reactions to important moments. arxiv.title: Luggage re-identification: A study of strategies towards a real-world application
arxiv.abstract: Luggage re-identification (ReID) is a critical task in video surveillance for forensics, security or border management (suspicious or abandoned luggage recognition), as well as luggage management (lost luggage recovery). It enables the association of observations of the same luggage across disjoint camera views in complex environments such as airports, train stations and border crossing. While exi

arxiv.title: SonoWorld4D: From One Video to a 4D Audio-Visual Scene via Diffusion Synchronization
arxiv.abstract: Recent progress in visual scene generation has extended beyond static 3D scenes toward the more challenging problem of generating dynamic 4D scenes from minimal input. However, sound, despite being intrinsically coupled with dynamic objects and events, remains largely unmodeled in prior work. We introduce Video-to-4DAVScene, a new task that turns a video into an explorable, time-varying 4D audio-v

arxiv.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
arxiv.abstract: An observer sees only part of the surrounding world, yet must keep track of what lies beyond the current view. Spatial perception therefore involves more than recognizing individual images: it calls for a persistent spatial state that is updated under self-motion and used to guide action. Do visual foundation models provide representations that support such a state? We study this question through

arxiv.abstract: As robots and intelligent systems increasingly interact with humans, they must anticipate long sequences of future actions from only brief observations. While purely neural models typically require extensive observations to predict future actions and remain difficult to interpret and adjust, symbolic priors offer a structured alternative. arxiv.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
arxiv.abstract: Interactive world models generate visual content conditioned on user actions, yet maintaining spatial consistency over long-horizon exploration in real time remains challenging. Existing approaches rely on either temporal context or explicit 3D memory, both of which scale poorly because memory grows with the length of the generated stream. arxiv.title: Fight World Model: Customizable Combat through Visual Interaction Proxies
arxiv.abstract: A playable, programmable game world must maintain persistent state, enforce executable rules, and support extensible gameplay mechanics. Existing video world models can generate plausible combat, yet struggle to keep hit reactions and health updates consistent with game rules. We introduce Fight World Model (FWM), which separates rule-governed combat execution from video rendering. An executable e

arxiv.title: HairDeck: Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from a Single Image
arxiv.abstract: The hair of stylized characters in games and avatars is built from hair cards: artist-placed ribbons whose geometry is the visible hair, animated by spring bones. Existing image-based methods produce realistic hair or a single fused mesh, while CHARM, the only generator of stylized hair cards, decodes a hairstyle autoregressively as a long sequence of control points. Observing that a card hairstyl

arxiv.title: Beyond Ground Truth: A Heuristic Unsupervised Quality Assurance Engine for Diagnosing Calibrational Blindness in Dental Segmentation
arxiv.abstract: In real-world clinical settings, dental X-ray segmentation using deep learning methods suffers from reliability issues. Even when the segmentation quality is bad, deep learning models show high confidence in their predictions (calibrational blindness). Moreover, in real use, doctors do not have ground-truth masks to check their accuracy. To address this problem, we introduce a simple quality-check

arxiv.title: RADIOlogy: A Single-Pass Approach to Training-Free Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection
arxiv.abstract: Current zero-shot anomaly detection methods often rely on complex prompt-learning techniques or computationally expensive sliding-window strategies to achieve fine-grained visual alignment to detect small-scale anomalies. This reliance stems from the fundamental limitation of standard CLIP architectures, where [CLS] token attention and spatial patch pooling struggle to capture subtle, localized an

arxiv.title: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents
arxiv.abstract: Building and scaling computer-using agents (CUAs) across desktop, mobile, and web environments requires reliable task-completion verification for data curation, evaluation, and reinforcement learning. Typical automated approaches prompt vision-language models (VLMs) to judge trajectories or generate programs to inspect application state. However, both rely on partial views of complex digital envir

arxiv.title: PhysCount: Do MLLMs Count Visual Appearances or Physical Entities?
arxiv.abstract: Images reveal appearances, but counting often asks about physical objects. A single entity may be visible directly, in several reflections, or through glass, so detecting every visible occurrence does not determine how many entities are present. Existing visual counting benchmarks rarely separate these two operations. We introduce PhysCount, a benchmark for evaluating whether multimodal large lang

hf_papers.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
hf_papers.abstract: This survey unifies video understanding and generation through world modeling, organizing progress around inferring, synthesizing, sharing, and interacting with latent temporal states to emphasize persistent dynamics over clip-level perception.

hf_papers.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
hf_papers.abstract: PDRVLA improves robot action generation by integrating a lightweight physical dynamics module that predicts future visual features with world-model supervision, avoiding online video generation latency.

hf_papers.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
hf_papers.abstract: InteractiveWorld provides a verifiable simulation environment and benchmark to evaluate whether multimodal language models can reliably guide humans through physical tasks.

hf_papers.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
hf_papers.abstract: Hy-Nomas is a video world model that uses causal attention and structured conditioning to generate interactive, multi-turn video segments with text and camera control.

hf_papers.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
hf_papers.abstract: Rollback improves robot policies by using world models to rewind to past decisions, explore counterfactual actions, and generate fine-grained supervision, while continuously refining dynamics via real-world feedback.

hf_papers.title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents
hf_papers.abstract: UserArena introduces a real-world interactive benchmark with long-horizon shopping trajectories and an evaluation framework, alongside On-Policy Trajectory Distillation to improve simulator fidelity for agentic recommendations.

hf_papers.title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
hf_papers.abstract: HiSTEVE is a hierarchical vision-language-action agent that combines long-horizon planning with native keyboard-and-mouse control to perform complex open-ended tasks in Minecraft.

hf_papers.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain
hf_papers.abstract: RynnUnify is a 16B unified embodied model that integrates visual planning, physical reasoning, and robot control, achieving state-of-the-art results on long-horizon embodied tasks.

hf_papers.title: AV-FABLE: Audio-Visual Manipulation Forensics in Long-Form Videos
hf_papers.abstract: AV-FABLE introduces a long-form audio-visual benchmark for sparse manipulations, showing that frozen perception features of audio-visual large language models contain forensic evidence best recovered via separate temporal decoders rather than language outputs.

hf_papers.title: World-in-Context: Interactive Video World Modeling with In-Context Conditioning
hf_papers.abstract: World-in-Context unifies view, action, and camera controls via explicit tokens and interaction-aware positional encoding to improve interactive video generation and navigation.

hf_papers.title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
hf_papers.abstract: Dual Exam evaluates multimodal agents and world models separately across diverse domains, revealing uneven performance and no coupled success in pilot tests.

hf_papers.title: DiscoDemo: Discovering Efficient and Diverse Robot Demonstrations for Imitation Learning
hf_papers.abstract: DiscoDemo uses reinforcement learning to generate diverse successful robot manipulation trajectories for training more robust visuomotor imitation policies.

hf_papers.title: RynnVLA-Latent: Scaling Robotic Manipulation Foundation Models with 3D-Grounded Latent Actions
hf_papers.abstract: RynnVLA-Latent leverages latent actions derived from diverse video to pretrain large vision-language-action policies, achieving high success across simulated and real-world robot benchmarks without embodiment-specific tuning.

hf_papers.title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Action Models
hf_papers.abstract: RoboHarness enables LLM agents to perform embodied manipulation via a visual-geometric control interface, surpassing specialized vision-language-action models on robotics benchmarks.

hf_papers.title: FocusVLA: Future-Intent Guided Dynamic View Routing for Vision-Language-Action Models
hf_papers.abstract: FocusVLA improves robotic manipulation by dynamically routing between global and local camera views based on predicted interaction intent across task stages.

hf_papers.title: FLOMSS: Generative Music Source Separation by Flow Matching
hf_papers.abstract: Flow matching is investigated for four-source full-band stereo music separation, evaluating prediction targets, flow paths, modeling strategies, and consistency constraints with both signal-level and perceptual metrics.

hf_papers.title: Echo: Coupled Action and Task Status Signal Denoising for Vision Language Action Models
hf_papers.abstract: Echo integrates stop and failure signals into a vision-language-action model to guide robot execution and recovery without fine-grained progress labels.

hf_papers.title: WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One Agent From Narration to Long-Form Video
hf_papers.abstract: WeVisCut is a script-to-video system that trains a compact policy to coordinate video editing tools, recover from failures, and reduce token usage while maintaining quality.

hf_papers.title: HuGe: Scaling Humanoid Generalist Vision-Language-Action Models with Egocentric Experience
hf_papers.abstract: HuGe pre-trains vision-language-action models on egocentric human and robot data with pseudo-proprioception and visual adaptation to enable whole-body humanoid control.

hf_papers.title: Evaluating DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks
hf_papers.abstract: Independent safety evaluation of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 reveals substantial improvements over prior versions and near-parity with leading closed-source models, while recommending process-level observability, incremental safety testing, and private benchmarks.

hf_papers.title: OpenFlyV2: An onboard vision-language-action model for aerial perception and navigation
hf_papers.abstract: OpenFlyV2 is a unified onboard vision-language-action model that enables real-time aerial navigation and reasoning on resource-constrained hardware using shared multimodal representations.

hf_papers.title: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation
hf_papers.abstract: A simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation on low-cost robot arms reveals that hybrid LLM agents outperform learned vision-language-action policies, with ranking consistency between simulation and real hardware.

highlights: PDRVLA 以轻量物理动力学表征监督未来视觉特征预测，在不进行在线视频生成的前提下增强机器人动作生成：[端到端VLA]
Gym-Anything 以数字智能体扩展物理仿真构建，直指高保真机器人训练环境的生产瓶颈：[控制层·世界模型]
Genie 4 获 HN 1,041 分关注，代表实时世界模拟向更强真实感与可交互性推进：[控制层·世界模型]

items.title: PDRVLA：以物理动力学表征增强动作生成
items.summary: 在 VLA 中引入轻量物理动力学模块，以世界模型监督预测未来视觉特征，避免在线视频生成带来的控制时延。[端到端VLA]

items.title: RynnVLA-Latent：3D 接地潜动作扩展操作基础模型
items.summary: 从多样视频中导出潜动作预训练大规模机器人策略，并以相机补偿 3D 流等监督提高跨仿真与真机基准的泛化；代码已公开。[端到端VLA]

items.title: HuGe：第一视角经验扩展人形通用 VLA
items.summary: 结合第一视角人类与机器人数据、伪本体感觉状态和视觉适配，面向人形机器人的全身闭环控制；代码已公开。[端到端VLA]

items.title: SwapBot：可换工具与触觉感知的机器人操作
items.summary: 面向切、刷、放置等接触丰富的日常任务，研究机器人自主更换并使用合适末端工具，结合触觉感知处理多样接触交互。[控制层·BC]

items.title: DAWN：扩散式对准与拆卸工作流
items.summary: 以多模态感知和分层扩散框架处理真实世界紧固件拆卸，将精确对准与操作流程统一到自动化工作流中。[控制层·扩散]

items.title: DEED：示范扩展提升精细操作
items.summary: 通过结构化扩展示范并重新设计执行环节，适配预训练 VLA 到 MetaFine 五项精细操作任务，兼顾视觉变化鲁棒性与精确控制。[控制层·BC]

items.title: Genie 4：新一代实时世界模拟
items.summary: Google DeepMind 发布的世界模型主打实时模拟与更高真实感，HN 获 1,041 分关注；其机器人训练与迁移价值仍需后续公开评测验证。[控制层·世界模型]

items.title: Gym-Anything：用数字智能体规模化物理仿真
items.summary: 针对高质量机器人仿真依赖专家手工构建、难以扩展的问题，提出借助数字智能体扩展物理模拟覆盖面，为 sim2real 数据飞轮提供路径。[控制层·世界模型]

items.title: InteractiveWorld：可验证的人类物理任务交互环境
items.summary: 提供可验证仿真环境与基准，评估多模态模型能否可靠地闭环指导人类完成物理任务；代码已公开。[规划层]

domains.name: 具身模型（感知/规划/控制三层 × 动作生成方式）

items.title: Rollback：在世界模型中回溯经验改进策略
items.summary: 让机器人策略回到过去决策点探索反事实动作，生成细粒度监督，并用真实世界反馈持续修正动力学模型。[控制层·世界模型]

items.title: CoAWM：跨本体连续动作世界模型
items.summary: 学习跨本体、跨执行频率的时空动力学先验，以共享潜函数空间表示机器人动作，并通过两阶段训练支持动作生成。[控制层·世界模型]

items.title: RynnUnify：统一具身大脑
items.summary: 16B 模型结合视频—语言推理、物理预测和机器人控制，面向长视野具身任务的统一视觉规划与行动建模；代码已公开。[控制层·世界模型]

items.title: PhysVLMM：面向可动部件的物理信念地图
items.summary: 在视觉—语言—运动地图中维护门、抽屉等可动部件对拉拽交互的物理信念，供规划器查询和更新。[感知层]

domains.name: 具身智能芯片（机器人计算 / 边缘 NPU）
